description: Blades hang in gleaming rows along oak-panelled walls, each with a small card describing it in the hushed language of a wine list. A sign over the counter reads: YOU BEND IT, YOU BOUGHT IT. YOU BLEED ON IT, YOU ALSO BOUGHT IT. A second, smaller sign adds that the management buys as well as sells, at prices it describes as 'fair' and its customers describe as 'half'.

doorways.description: Back across the street to the Watch House.

stock.name: a serviceable dagger
stock.description: The card says 'ideal for the beginner'. It does not say beginner at what.

stock.name: a stout oak cudgel
stock.description: A length of seasoned oak with a leather wrist-loop. No moving parts, no instructions, no complaints so far.

stock.name: a short sword
stock.description: Plain, sharp, and honest, which makes it the only thing in Ankh-Morpork that is all three.

stock.name: a hunting spear
stock.description: Ash shaft, leaf-shaped head, and a balance that suggests it would much rather be somewhere else, quickly.

stock.name: a dwarfish battle-axe
stock.description: Double-headed and heavy enough to settle most arguments by being put down on the table. The maker's rune translates roughly as 'you're welcome'.
